So ref [6] is cited as an example of sensor-enhanced interfaces. Need see if cited paper supports that. Cited paper is Cabi et al. reward sketching and batch RL. It uses teleoperation, vision, proprioception, multiple cameras, force-torque sensor? It is about data-driven robotics with reward sketching and batch RL, not sensor-enhanced interfaces. It does use sensors (cameras, proprioception, wrist force-torque sensor) but the category "sensor-enhanced interfaces" likely refers to interfaces enhanced by sensors? Need decide. The cited paper is not about sensor-enhanced interfaces; it's about reward sketching/batch RL. It may be incorrectly cited. Need quote from cited paper that contradicts or shows about something else. Need exact quote max 60 words. We can quote abstract: "By harnessing a growing dataset of robot experience, we learn control policies for a diverse and increasing set of related manipulation tasks. To make this possible, we introduce reward sketching..." This shows it's about reward sketching and batch RL, not sensor-enhanced interfaces. Or quote "This paper presents a data-driven approach to apply deep RL effectively to learn to perform manipulation tasks on real robots from vision." Need status incorrect. Reason: FastUMI cites it as sensor-enhanced interface, but paper is about reward sketching and batch RL from stored data; not an interface category. Need ensure quote verbatim from cited text. Use exact passage. Need JSON only. Need include claim one sentence. "FastUMI relies on reference [6] as an example of sensor-enhanced interfaces for robot learning." Status incorrect. Or include "At its heart are three important ideas: (i) efficient elicitation of user preferences to learn reward functions, (ii) automatic annotation of all historical data with any of the learned reward functions, and (iii) harnessing the large annotated datasets to learn policies purely from stored data via batch RL." That's 40 words. Better quote shows not sensor-enhanced. Need exact from text: "This paper presents a data-driven approach to apply deep RL effectively to learn to perform manipulation tasks on real robots from vision." Yes.
